exposure: Frozen repair-jobs and original source references read. No lead returned-image verdict supplied before inspection. Prior independent primary concerns and the19 identity repair brief are known.
phone_scope: Five actual390x844 read-only history screenshots; full1536x1024 boards rendered338x225.33, slightly smaller than360px primary gallery. No voting controls or selection changes.

observations: The harpoon point now has a visible top margin and both soles remain framed. The free hand visibly holds the large terminal ring, while portrait face, costume and matte paint remain recognizably Eris.

The tether is not one continuous outside-leg arc: the harpoon-side chain descends to the left boot/ankle and appears to terminate against it; a separate chain runs from the free-hand ring to a loose end on the ground at far right. The original boot-contact defect persists and continuity is worse.
Phone retains attractive portrait and clearer point margin, but also the two separated dangling chain paths. Larger independent hand/ring visibility is not proof of an integrated weapon.
05-C2.artistic_appeal_change: Portrait and character appeal broadly preserved; new chain layout makes the full-figure weapon read less coherently.
remaining_failures: Single continuous harpoon-to-ring tether is not visible.
Harpoon butt attachment is partly obscured by the hip panel.

observations: The arm pose changes and the upper string is visible, while the severe mature portrait, cutout bronze bow and dense curved engraving remain coherent.

The string still does not follow upper tip to drawing fingers to lower tip. The upper-tip line meets a diagonal near the support forearm; that diagonal runs between drawing-hand area and riser/grip, producing a Y-like crossing. No clear string segment reaches the lower bow tip.
Phone preserves face and bow silhouette but reduces the crossing to a small confusing junction; no image-scale evidence establishes the required single clean V.
15-C2.artistic_appeal_change: Regal face and engraved finish survive; the new pose does not supply convincing bow control.
remaining_failures: Drawing fingers are not the sole apex of two taut tip-connected segments.

observations: Drawing hand moves up near the loaded pouch/stone and the sling silhouette opens into a clearer aiming pose. Support hand visibly grips the Y handle; bob-haired face, costume and clear-line treatment persist.

Both elastic bands attach to the same left/upper fork limb: one at its tip and one farther down that limb. The opposite right fork tip has a wrap but no band connecting it to the pouch. This replaces the original loading ambiguity with a clear attachment failure.
Phone shows the aiming gesture and small pouch at the hand, yet the empty opposite fork and same-limb band endpoints remain apparent. Correct pouch location alone does not fix the full implement.
17-C2.artistic_appeal_change: Poised adult charm and clean silhouette remain appealing; new aiming pose is stronger, but weapon function is not coherent.
remaining_failures: Two bands terminate on one fork limb.
Fine pinching-finger/stone detail is small on phone and not independently resolvable there.

observations: Weapon and raised hand are removed from the portrait, leaving an unobscured head/shoulder view. Adult face, athletic stance and fine manga hatching are retained.

In the full figure the fist wraps a vertical cylindrical grip, while the crescent blade sits beside it without a clearly visible connecting stalk. Removing the D-frame also removes the visible structural connection; the handle remains broadly parallel to the blade rather than a single perpendicular tonfa grip.

The blade still projects ahead of the arm rather than following its outside forearm with the requested tonfa relation. Phone preserves the clean portrait and crescent shape but cannot establish the missing connection. Red weapon-spine accent is also lost.
13-C2.artistic_appeal_change: Portrait hierarchy improves and character appeal survives, but the full-figure weapon now appears unsupported.
remaining_failures: Perpendicular tonfa handle/forearm relation not established.
Portrait hair still lacks the generous top margin.

observations: Both views change to short swept-back ash-blond hair and a broader lower face/jaw, shorter broader-tipped nose, straighter brows and changed lip balance. A small eyebrow notch is visible. This is more than a hair recolor and materially reduces the original-anchor resemblance.

Silky restrained facial modeling, pale/black/crimson organization, ivory sleeveless robe, continuous scythe grip and complete figure remain consistent. Incidental arm/waist chains are removed; portrait and figure broadly match the new identity.

The expression reads more self-assured and approachable than the primary dark-haired predatory model; that is a different appeal, not proof of owner preference. Brocade remains extensive and the decorative crescent at the scythe root remains despite the simplification request.
Phone retains the changed head/hair construction and complete scythe silhouette. Pale face and blade details are delicate, but no major introduced anatomy, grip or framing regression is visible.
19-C1.artistic_appeal_change: Distinctly changed handsome adult presence with a slightly warmer crooked smile; refined19 rendering and combat identity retained.
remaining_failures: Robe surface pattern remains busy rather than fully simplified.
Originality is an informed comparative visual judgment, not proof against every possible existing design.

overall: 19-C1 shows material identity improvement without a major introduced regression. The four mechanical retries contain limited local gains but fail their complete target and retain or introduce substantial weapon-construction errors. This report does not select attempts.
